first.rationale: The two observed declines (onboarding completion -4%, activation -6%) are plausibly the same funnel problem, and memory_86 is the only inherited result that claims to move completion, time-to-value, and early adoption together, so it is the highest-leverage single slot. I want the archived record for memory_86 because it was consolidated on day 52 and completion has fallen since; if the original effect was small, short-horizon, or measured on a cohort unlike today's, the inherited summary is stale and my whole plan rests on it. I want memory_73 second because promotional pricing is the intuitive answer to a competitor's entry pricing and is the option I am most likely to be wrong to decline: the summary reports acquisition and revenue lift but says nothing about retention, margin, or whether the acquired accounts stayed qualified, which is exactly the gap that matters for a sustainable-revenue objective. Discount-led acquisition can post a strong quarter while importing a churn-prone, price-anchored cohort, so I will not run it on an unverified summary. Downstream value risk on my own chosen action too: 'simplify' and 'shorten' can mean removing steps that actually deliver value or capture qualifying information. memory_31's field-cutting result improved activation but fewer signup fields can degrade lead routing and starve the sales-assisted enterprise path in memory_44, which means a completion-rate win could quietly cost qualified pipeline. So I am scoping this as a small guarded test with a holdout, instrumented on downstream qualified revenue and retention rather than completion alone, and I am cutting friction that is not information-bearing rather than dropping qualification fields. memory_91 stays the fallback if verification shows memory_86 was weak or narrow, since activation messaging is additive and does not remove funnel steps. I am treating all of these as unverified priors, not settled facts, until the archive comes back.
